extracted.intended_audience: business and financial journalists, editors, and reporters
extracted.subtask_description: A practitioner-oriented rubric for evaluating and producing business/finance news stories that emphasizes a single defining number, proper numeric framing, and preference for structural, explanatory reporting over ephemeral market chatter.

rubrics_metrics.name: The number that matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Every business story should have a single defining figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify one headline number that encapsulates the story. Use that figure as the central hook and ensure subsequent analysis revolves around explaining its meaning and provenance rather than sprinkling many undifferentiated metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame ratios or comparisons that reframe a story by making its implications non-obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer comparisons and ratios (e.g., per-capita, percent-of-GDP, price-to-earnings) that change how readers interpret raw numbers. Use counter-intuitive framings to surface insight rather than merely restating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregated-vs-anecdotal trade-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer aggregate data, but allow anecdotes to illustrate aggregate patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on representative, aggregated evidence for claims; use anecdotes sparingly to humanize or illustrate a point but not to substitute for aggregate proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish flow vs. stock stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between flow measures (rates, changes) and stock measures (totals) and choose the appropriate framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit whether a metric reflects a flow or a stock; normalize or convert when necessary so readers understand whether they're seeing a level or a change over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about 'biggest ever' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat 'biggest ever' or superlative claims with suspicion and adjust for context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for inflation, population or market growth, and other baselines before accepting 'biggest' statements. Recast in real terms or per-unit terms when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware single-data-point trend pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid building trend narratives from a single data point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require corroborating data or longer-term context before declaring trends; show historical series or confidence intervals to support directional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the headline number meaningful in context?
rubrics_metrics.description: A headline figure must be interpretable and significant once contextualized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide baselines, comparators, or proportions so the headline number isn't misleading. Context can include historical averages, market size, or scale adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has the writer adjusted for size, growth, baseline?
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure numbers are normalized for size, growth, and relevant baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use per-capita, per-dollar, inflation-adjusted, or otherwise scaled metrics so comparisons are apples-to-apples; call out when raw totals distort the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the metric tell the story or just illustrate it?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the chosen metric is central to the argument or merely decorative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the metric isn't central, either pick a more telling one or recast the piece as illustration. Avoid metrics that merely dress up a narrative without changing its substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the framing pro-cyclical with the news cycle, or independent?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the story's framing is simply riding short-term news momentum or identifies an independent, structural insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer framings that reveal structural significance rather than reactive, pro-cyclical angles that echo immediate market moves without deeper explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize quiet structural shifts in financial markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevate stories that reveal underlying, lasting changes in market structure or behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for slow-moving but consequential changes (e.g., new clearing arrangements, shifts in market participants) that have long-term implications rather than transient events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation studies require proper baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat compensation research as strong when it uses correct baselines and comparators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate pay studies by whether they control for roles, hours, firm size, geography, and other relevant baselines; avoid raw comparisons that ignore these factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor counterintuitive macro pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote macroeconomic stories that overturn expectations through careful numeric framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward pieces that challenge conventional wisdom with robust data treatment and surprising but well-supported comparisons or normalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form on industries undergoing transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Value in-depth, long-form reporting on industries in flux.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support explanatory narratives that combine numbers, history, and on-the-ground reporting to show how and why an industry is changing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-English explanations of complex instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevate explainers that demystify complex financial instruments for general readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate jargon into accessible language, use clear examples and well-chosen numbers, and ensure the reader understands risks, mechanics, and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote day-to-day market chatter
rubrics_metrics.description: Downrank routine market noise and ephemeral daily moves as low-value coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid stories that only report daily price movements without deeper analysis of causes, context, or significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Stocks did X today because Y' narratives are weak
rubrics_metrics.description: Skepticism toward simple causal stories tying a single day's market move to an attributed reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demand evidence beyond anecdote for causal attributions of daily market moves; explore broader patterns or structural drivers instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote rich-list voyeurism
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid coverage that serves only as celebrity/wealth gawking without analytic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat lists of wealthy individuals or rankings as low-priority unless they illuminate broader economic or policy questions with proper numeric framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reproducing hype cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not perpetuate technology or market hype without critical numeric scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question optimistic claims, check unit economics and adoption rates, and show what assumptions underlie enthusiasm before amplifying a hype narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeracy as a newsworthiness criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Business newsworthiness should require numeric integrity — stories must 'add up' before they 'go up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat numeracy (correct metrics, proper normalization, meaningful comparisons) as a threshold for story selection and framing; numerical care is a journalistic standard, not optional ornamentation.
